constraint_prompts.purpose: the poem's own lines are verified and timed to this reel
constraint_prompts.prompt: Now go, they tell me. To ask if I can inherit the earth — to ask if I can name my own stars. Even galaxies, if I may. The past, too, was waiting for me — coming of age in the shared rooms of humid basements as bedrooms; mattress pads where the wood beams of Southern pine could comfort my spine. It didn’t. To dream was to prevail. They tell me: ask if I can invent a new universe — if God would let me, little ole me, award a blessing here and there. Even grant miracles. In uncertain times, in forsaken times. Their blood flows through my hands — fingerprints that orchestra great powers — sun-kissing my skin, deepening my voice to a baritone of a million cries. Beware of me. The gates open with wings — gifted from evolution, and made of marble stones kissed by the hymns our Creator composed, with an orchestra of our ancestors’ wildest dreams, to welcome us.

failure_risks: disocclusion holes where back-paint is thin
